terms.gloss: estimate, value, put a figure on
terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation, transitive; the value in the genitive or ablative
evidence: Cic. Dom. 44 (Lewis & Short): domum ēmit prope dīmidiō cārius quam aestimābat
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to determine or estimate the extrinsic (money) value of a thing, to value, rate, appraise”. For “think, reckon”, use exīstimāre or putāre, which Lewis & Short sets apart from it.

evidence: Cato Agr. 2.2 (Lewis & Short): ratiōnem inīre oportet operārum, diērum
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to make an estimate”. For a rough figure Latin adds circiter or ferē. Lewis & Short: “to cast up, reckon, calculate” (Caes. BG 7.71.4); Traupman also uses it for “take steps, take measures”, which we have not found in Lewis & Short.

evidence: Liv. 39.6.9: vīlissimum antīquīs mancipium et aestimātiōne et ūsū

phrases.latin: rūmōrēsque senum sevēriōrum omnēs ūnius aestimēmus assis
phrases.english: and let us value all the gossip of stern old men at a single penny

phrases.latin: tum coquus, vīlissimum antīquīs mancipium et aestimātiōne et ūsū, in pretiō esse, et quod ministerium fuerat, ars habērī coepta
phrases.english: Then the cook, to our forefathers the cheapest of slaves both in value and in use, began to be prized, and what had been a menial job came to be thought an art.
What do you think this house is worth?
to take steps, to take measures

sources: Lewis & Short: aestimo · Lewis & Short: ineo · Lewis & Short: aestimatio · Lewis & Short: ratio
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 323, checked against the searchable text of the book (9 November 2026).
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-catullus, loci-livius), checked against the editions named there.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
